items.title: Disk bundle, sphere bundle, and Thom space: the differential topology interface
items.statement: For a supplied metric $h$ on a finite-rank real vector bundle $E\to B$, $D_h(E)=\{v:\|v\|_h\le1\}$, $S_h(E)=\{v:\|v\|_h=1\}$ and $\operatorname{Th}_h(E)=D_h(E)/S_h(E)$, with $X/\varnothing=X_+$. This is the DT notation for the published metric disk/sphere/Thom quotient: the complement of the basepoint is the open disk bundle, identified with $E$ by fiberwise radial expansion and carrying its smooth structure when $E$ is smooth; no smooth manifold structure at the Thom basepoint is presumed.
items.strategy: Restate the published definition and its based convention verbatim, fix the rank-zero and empty-base readings, and record that only the non-basepoint stratum is treated smoothly. The item defines notation and proves nothing; no choice is used.

items.title: Metric independence of the Thom space
items.statement: For two supplied metrics $h,k$ on one bundle, radial rescaling gives a canonical based homeomorphism $\operatorname{Th}_h(E)\cong\operatorname{Th}_k(E)$, and these maps compose exactly: $r_{k,l}r_{h,k}=r_{h,l}$.
items.strategy: Define $r_{h,k}(v)=(\|v\|_h/\|v\|_k)v$ off the zero section, prove continuity at $0$ by local equivalence of the two norms, descend to the based quotient, verify the composition law and exhibit the metric-interpolation isotopy.

items.title: Trivial Thom spaces as suspension smash products
items.statement: For $r\ge0$, with the product metric and the supplied trivialization, $\operatorname{Th}(B\times\mathbb R^r)\cong B_+\wedge S^r=\Sigma^rB_+$ naturally in $B$; the rank-zero and empty-base cases are included.
items.strategy: Identify the disk/sphere pair as $(B\times D^r,B\times S^{r-1})$, compare its quotient with the smash quotient through the universal property, and invoke the published trivial-bundle computation for the degeneracies; this is the AT result restated for the framed DT target.

items.title: Empty-base and rank-zero Thom conventions
items.statement: $\operatorname{Th}(0_B)=B_+$, even though the sphere bundle is empty; for $B=\varnothing$ the Thom space is the one-point space; a rank-zero collapse of a union of components is the identity on that union and sends the other components to the basepoint.
items.strategy: Record the consequences of the based quotient convention and the trivial-bundle proposition; no proof is required.

items.title: Stable normal bundle of a compact smooth manifold
items.statement: For a supplied smooth embedding $i:M\hookrightarrow\mathbb R^N$ of a compact smooth manifold, $\nu_i=i^*T\mathbb R^N/di(TM)$; a Euclidean metric identifies it with the orthogonal complement and gives $TM\oplus\nu_i\cong\varepsilon^N$ under countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, inherited from the published identification. The stable normal bundle is the class of these bundles under adding trivial real summands, and a normal structure includes its specified identification; a framing is an actual trivialization, not stable triviality alone.
items.strategy: Cite the published normal quotient and the ambient-metric identification under their recorded countable-choice hypothesis, declare that inheritance, and form the stabilization class. No unstable cancellation and no additional choice are asserted.

items.title: Stable normal bundle is independent of the embedding
items.statement: Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, inherited from the normal-bundle identifications. For embeddings $i_j:M\hookrightarrow\mathbb R^{N_j}$ of a compact smooth manifold, $\nu_{i_0}\oplus\varepsilon^{N_1}\cong\nu_{i_1}\oplus\varepsilon^{N_0}$; hence the stable normal class is intrinsic. The same assertion holds for compact manifolds with boundary.
items.strategy: Use the smooth rotation j_t=(cos(pi t/2)i0,sin(pi t/2)i1) in the common ambient sum. Orthogonal tangent projections Q_t are smooth by the full-rank frame formula; P_t=I-Q_t projects onto normals, with im(P0)=nu_i0⊕epsilon_N1 and im(P1)=epsilon_N0⊕nu_i1. The skew commutator K=dot(P)P-Pdot(P) has [K,P]=dot(P); its unique smooth linear ODE transport U conjugates P0 to P_t, restricting to normal images. Reorder the endpoint summands, retain unstable ranks and boundary charts. Identical embeddings do not make this rotating path constant.

items.title: Compatible tubular charts realize a prescribed normal identification
items.statement: Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $i:S\hookrightarrow M$ be a closed smooth embedded submanifold, $E\to S$ a smooth rank-$r$ bundle and $\alpha:E\to\nu(S)=i^*TM/di(TS)$ a smooth bundle isomorphism over $\mathrm{id}_S$. Then some diffeomorphism $\Phi$ of a neighbourhood of the zero section $0_S$ in $E$ onto a neighbourhood of $i(S)$ in $M$, with $\Phi(s,0)=i(s)$, induces exactly $\alpha$ on the normal quotient; in particular, with $E=\nu(S)$ and $\alpha=\mathrm{id}$ the normal bundle admits a chart inducing the identity. Compatibility fixes the induced normal derivative, not merely the zero section.
items.strategy: Use one tubular chart Φ₀ from the published theorem and the induced normal map β₀ of a zero-fixing chart: local frames make β₀ a smooth bundle automorphism of ν(S), so Φ₀∘β₀^{-1}∘α is the required compatible chart. AC_ω is used exactly for the tubular chart and a Riemannian metric exhibiting the smooth normal structure.

items.title: Pontryagin–Thom collapse with specified normal data
items.statement: Let $S\subset X$ be a compact embedded smooth submanifold without boundary of codimension $r$ in a smooth boundaryless manifold, with a specified smooth rank-$r$ bundle $E\to S$ and smooth isomorphism $\alpha:E\to TX|_S/TS$. A compatible tubular chart is a diffeomorphism $\Phi$ of a neighborhood of $0_S$ in $E$ onto a neighborhood of $S$ inducing exactly $\alpha$ on the normal quotient; the compatible-chart lemma supplies such charts under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ (the only choice used). For a smooth metric and radius $\rho$ with $\Phi$ defined near $D_\rho(E)$, the collapse $c_{\Phi,\rho}:X_+\to\operatorname{Th}(E)$ sends $\Phi(s,v)$, $\|v\|<\rho$, to the class of $(s,v/\rho)$ and all other points to the basepoint; for locally compact $X$ the same formula defines $c:X^+\to\operatorname{Th}(E)$.
items.strategy: Define the specified normal-data compatibility condition so that the induced normal derivative is the given $\alpha$ (fixing the zero section alone is insufficient), then define the collapse through the quotient model. The inherited countable choice is used exactly for the existence of compatible charts.

items.title: Continuity and smooth local representatives of collapse
items.statement: The defined collapse is continuous and based; its restriction over the complement of the Thom basepoint is smooth, it is smooth near the zero section with zero a regular value in every normal fiber chart, and radial cutoff models give based homotopic collapses with any prescribed positive linear normal scale near zero.
items.strategy: Paste the closed tube and the closed complement of its interior over the finite closed cover of $X$; compute the vertical derivative $\rho^{-1}\alpha^{-1}$ to get smoothness and regularity near $S$; interpolate radial profiles convexly to obtain the cutoff representatives and their based homotopy.

items.title: Collapse homotopy for a fixed normal identification
items.statement: For compact $S\subset X$ and fixed specified normal data $(E,\alpha)$, collapses formed from any two compatible tubular charts, positive sufficiently small radii and supplied metrics represent the same based homotopy class after the canonical radial identification of the metric targets. Compatibility means identity induced normal derivative relative to $\alpha$; precomposition by an arbitrary normal bundle automorphism is not an auxiliary tubular choice and need not preserve the class.
items.strategy: For the chart transition $\psi=\Phi_1^{-1}\Phi_0$, rescale $\psi_t=\delta_{1/t}\psi\delta_t$; Taylor's integral formula extends $\psi_t$ smoothly to the identity at $t=0$ because the induced normal derivative is $I$, and the same formula for $\psi^{-1}$ gives a uniform compact tube. Collapse along $\Phi_1\psi_t$ and interpolate the radii and metrics; a reflected normal line gives opposite degrees and shows the compatibility hypothesis is essential.

items.strategy: Interior/boundaryless transverse preimage and differential normal quotient; with boundary transversality, use a smooth Euclidean inverse-function chart (h,remaining tangential coordinates,t), preserving the boundary time coordinate exactly. Global normal isomorphism restricts to boundary normal data. Zero section is closed in every rank; in rank zero B is clopen in B_+, and the purported interval counterexample is not continuous.

items.title: Transverse based homotopies give normal cobordisms
items.statement:
Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $E\to B$ be a smooth real vector bundle of rank $r\ge0$. Let $X$ be a compact smooth manifold without boundary and $H:X\times I\to\operatorname{Th}(E)$ a based homotopy constant in the time variable on neighbourhoods of $t=0$ and $t=1$.

(a) If $H$ is smooth on an open neighbourhood of its zero-section preimage $W=H^{-1}(0_B)$ and transverse to the zero section there, then $W$ is a compact neat embedded submanifold of $X\times I$ with $\partial W=W_0\sqcup W_1$, where $W_i=H_i^{-1}(0_B)$, and the normal bundle of $W$ in $X\times I$ is identified with the pullback of $E$ along the base-coordinate map of $H$; thus $W$ is a compact normal cobordism between $W_0$ and $W_1$.

(b) If $H$ is merely continuous with $H_0,H_1$ smooth and transverse to the zero section near their zero preimages, then for every closed $F\subseteq X\times I$ with $F\cap W=\varnothing$ there is a based homotopy from $H_0$ to $H_1$, fixed on $X\times\{0\}$ and $X\times\{1\}$ and pointwise on $F$, which is smooth and transverse to the zero section near its own zero preimage; only a neighbourhood of the zero section is smoothed or perturbed, and the Thom basepoint need not be smooth.
items.strategy: All-rank construction: rank zero has W=W0×I clopen and uses relative smooth approximation into B on an extended time interval, pasted with the unchanged basepoint. Positive rank uses a compact closed central time band, overlapping smooth endpoint collars protected by relative approximation, a compact relevant zero-free buffer, and compactly supported smoothing. Actual vertically submersive family gives cutoff-scaled transversality. Choose a good parameter inside a genuinely small safety ball; use the full smooth formula at eta=0 and open-cover gluing outside compact support. F and endpoints stay fixed, basepoint is never smoothed, arbitrary noncompact B and empty zero sets included.

items.title: The Thom quotient identifies relative and reduced cohomology
items.statement:
Let $E\to B$ be a finite-rank real vector bundle with a supplied continuous
fibre metric, and put $D=D_h(E)$, $S=S_h(E)$ and $Y=D/S$ with the based
empty-subspace convention of
[[def-disk-sphere-and-thom-space-of-a-metric-vector-bundle]]. For every
abelian coefficient group $G$ and integer $k$, the quotient map of pairs
$q:(D,S)\to(Y,\{*\})$ induces a natural isomorphism
$$q^*:\widetilde H^k(Y;G)\xrightarrow{\cong}H^k(D,S;G).$$
Here reduced cohomology is identified with cohomology relative to the supplied
basepoint. In rank zero this is the canonical isomorphism
$\widetilde H^k(B_+;G)\cong H^k(B;G)$, and an empty base gives zero groups.
The assertion holds for the ordinary based quotient and its compactly
generated version; it requires no choice beyond the supplied metric.
items.strategy: Prove the actual quotient pullback on cohomology: sphere neighbourhood strong radial retraction; natural cohomology pair-sequence and Five Lemma replace sphere/point by their neighbourhoods; excision removes sphere and quotient point, and the remaining pairs are homeomorphic. Identify reduced cohomology with relative-to-basepoint groups including degree0. For empty sphere the clopen disjoint basepoint gives an explicit relative-chain/cochain isomorphism with the original base; kification preserves singular simplices. No Hom-exactness assumption, compact base, orientation or Choice beyond the supplied metric.

items.title: Thom class and Thom isomorphism: the AT interface
items.statement: Assume AC as in [[def-axiom-of-choice]]. Let $E\to B$ be an $R$-oriented numerable rank-$r$ real vector bundle over a CW complex, or over a paracompact Hausdorff base of CW type. Its AT Thom class is the unique $u_E\in H^r(D(E),S(E);R)$ of [[def-thom-class-by-fiberwise-normalization]], whose restriction to every oriented fiber disk pair is the supplied generator. In the based quotient model $D_h(E)/S_h(E)$ of [[def-disk-sphere-and-thom-space-of-a-metric-vector-bundle]] write the same class in $$\widetilde H^r(\operatorname{Th}_h(E);R)\cong H^r(D(E),S(E);R).$$ The isomorphism is the actual quotient-map pullback of [[lem-thom-disk-sphere-quotient-identifies-relative-and-reduced-cohomology]], proved there from the exact cohomology excision and natural pair-sequence interfaces, including reduced degree0 and the empty sphere case. In rank zero it reads $\widetilde H^k(B_+;R)\cong H^k(B;R)$ in every degree, with the supplied rank-zero orientation normalization. The AT theorem [[thm-thom-isomorphism-for-oriented-vector-bundles]] gives the isomorphism $a\mapsto\pi^*a\smile u_E$ from $H^k(B;R)$ onto $H^{k+r}(D(E),S(E);R)$ for all $k$, and [[thm-naturality-and-uniqueness-of-thom-classes]] gives uniqueness, oriented pullback naturality and integral sign reversal. For $R=\mathbb F_2$ the orientation is automatic. No Thom class and no Thom isomorphism is constructed again in DT: the collapse and duality statements below consume exactly this interface. On compact smooth bases the finite-cover AT proof is available choice-free once the cover and its data are supplied; references to the general supplier retain its stated AC assumption.
items.strategy: Consume the exact existing AT normalized Thom class and cup-product isomorphism. The new local cohomology quotient helper proves the canonical quotient pullback, including rank-zero B_+, reduced degree0 and empty base, from actual cohomological excision and LES suppliers. No homology-only theorem is asserted to prove a cohomology interface.

items.title: Collapse pulls the Thom class back to the Poincaré dual
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $i:S\hookrightarrow M$ be an embedding of closed smooth oriented manifolds, $r=\operatorname{codim}S$, and orient the normal bundle so that its orientation followed by that of $S$ orients $M|_S$. With the cohomology-first, front-evaluation cap convention, the collapse $c:M_+	o\operatorname{Th}(
u)$ satisfies $c^*u_
u\cap[M]=i_*[S]$ in $H_s(M;\mathbb Z)$, so $c^*u_
u=\operatorname{PD}_M(i_*[S])$. The same formula holds over $\mathbb F_2$ without orientations and over a commutative ring with compatible supplied orientations; rank zero uses component orientation generators.
items.strategy: Identify $c^*u_\nu$ with the compactly supported extension of the Thom class on the tube. Determine $p_*D_U(u)$ by its local generators: in an oriented normal-first product chart the fiber generator is normalized by the Thom interface, so front-evaluation cap by it retains the tangent generator; fundamental-class uniqueness then gives $D_U(u)=z_*[S]$. Compact-support duality and open-extension naturality yield the formula.

items.title: Adding a trivial normal line suspends the Thom space
items.statement: $\operatorname{Th}(E\oplus\varepsilon^1)\cong\operatorname{Th}(E)\wedge S^1=\Sigma\operatorname{Th}(E)$ naturally in bundle maps preserving the data; iterating adds one suspension per specified trivial normal direction.
items.strategy: Radially identify the sum-norm disk/sphere pair with the max-norm product pair. For nonempty S(E), the exact published CG k-product quotient theorem gives the smash quotient. In rank zero D/empty=B_+ is an adjoined basepoint, so use the explicit (B_+×I)/(B_+×boundaryI union {*}×I) presentation, not an onto map B→B_+. Empty base gives a point; metrics/trivialization preserving bundle maps commute with the radial formula.

items.title: Finite Thom spaces and the spectrum interface
items.statement: DT uses finite Thom spaces and the suspension identification to compare stabilized normal collapse data. Spectra, their structure maps and stable homotopy groups are owned by algebraic topology; no Thom spectrum is constructed or assumed here, and a stable normal bundle remains a finite bundle datum.
items.strategy: Record the ownership seam; no proof is required.

items.title: Thom space of a trivial line bundle
items.statement: For the supplied product line $B\times\mathbb R$, $\operatorname{Th}(B\times\mathbb R)=B_+\wedge S^1=\Sigma B_+$; for a point base this is $S^1$ and for empty base a point. The trivialization records which fiber direction is positive.
items.strategy: Compute the disk/sphere pair, collapse the interval quotient, and read off the cases from the trivial-rank proposition.

items.title: Möbius line Thom space as a projective-plane quotient
items.statement: For the Möbius line $L\to S^1$, $\operatorname{Th}(L)=D(L)/S(L)$ is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{RP}^2$ with the centre of a complementary disk as basepoint; equivalently it is the quotient $\mathbb{RP}^2/D^2$ whose complement is the interior of a Möbius band.
items.strategy: Realize $\mathbb{RP}^2$ by attaching a disk to the Möbius band boundary, collapse the attached disk, and use the radial collapse of an inner disk onto a slightly larger one to obtain a homeomorphism from the compact quotient to the Hausdorff projective plane.

items.title: Explicit normal-framed collapse of an equatorial sphere
items.statement: For the standard equator $S^n\subset S^{n+1}$ with its upward unit normal framing and $0<a<1$, $c(\sqrt{1-t^2}x,t)=[x,t/a]$ for $|t|<a$ and $c=*$ for $|t|\ge a$ defines the collapse to $S^n_+\wedge S^1$; projecting the first smash factor by $S^n_+\to S^0$ gives the framed collapse to $S^1$.
items.strategy: Verify the explicit band chart has the specified normal derivative, paste the constant complement continuously, and identify the target by the trivial-line proposition; $n=0$ is included.

items.title: Zero-section pullback is the Euler class
items.statement: Assume AC. For an oriented bundle in the AT Thom scope, $e(E)=s^*j^*u_E$: the zero-section pullback of the Thom class, through the relative-to-absolute map, is the Euler class. Rank zero with the standard orientation gives $e(0_B)=1$, and a positive-rank trivial bundle has $e=0$.
items.strategy: Identify the normalized classes of the interface and the Euler definition, compose the relative-to-absolute and zero-section maps, and for trivial bundles homotope the zero section to a unit-length section through the sphere boundary where $j^*u_E$ vanishes by pair exactness.

items.title: Embedding-dependent unstable normal Thom data
items.statement: It is false that the actual normal bundle, and its unsuspended Thom target, of a compact smooth manifold are independent of the embedding: the one-point manifold embedded in $\mathbb R$ and in $\mathbb R^2$ has normal fibers $\mathbb R$ and $\mathbb R^2$, whose Thom spaces $S^1$ and $S^2$ are not homeomorphic, while one stabilization identifies the bundles.
items.strategy: Compute the two normal fibers as quotients at a point, identify their Thom spaces as $S^1$ and $S^2$ by the trivial-bundle proposition, distinguish them by deletion properties, and observe compatibility with the stabilization theorem to show only the stable class is intrinsic.
